To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the synaptic terminals of fly photoreceptors are not required for the generation of the graded membrane potential (receptor potential); and (2) the synaptic terminals are not required for dark adaptation of the photoreceptor.
the electrical responses of intact photoreceptors lacking synapses are identical to normal receptor cells and that the photoreceptor responses are not affected by tetrodotoxine or carbon dioxide.

(i) photoreceptor cell development in flies is not dependent on synaptic activity and (ii) the responses of the intact photoreceptor cell can be generated without the feedback control of the optic lobe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the eye of the housefly, Musca domestica.
the properties of the intact photoreceptor cell of the housefly, Musca domestica.
the development of the visual system in insects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photoreceptors are able to function without synapses, but that the synapses are necessary for normal physiological function.
the photoreceptor membrane potential is not controlled by the optic lobe and that the synapses of photoreceptor cells in the optic lobe are not necessary for normal development of the receptor cells.
the receptor potential in flies is not a synaptic potential, but is a graded response of the receptor membrane to light, which spreads electrotonically to the soma and axon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photoreceptor membrane is the primary site of light detection and that the synapses of photoreceptors are not necessary for light adaptation or normal physiological function.
the photoreceptor cell of the fly eye is an autonomous, self-regulating system.
photoreceptor cells can function in the absence of synapses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the fly, the photoreceptors can generate their own receptor potentials without the need for feedback from the optic lomb.
the photoreceptor cell is a very simple and robust structure that can generate graded responses to light without the need for synaptic input from other cells.
the synaptic input to the photoreceptor cell body is not required for the normal development of the electrical properties of the receptor cells.
